```sql
WITH tenant_customers AS (
    SELECT c.id,
           c.email,
           c.company,
           c.country_code
      FROM customers c
     WHERE c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
),
paid_orders AS (
    SELECT o.customer_id,
           o.total_cents,
           o.created_at
      FROM orders o
      JOIN tenant_customers tc ON tc.id = o.customer_id
     WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
agg AS (
    SELECT po.customer_id,
           sum(po.total_cents) AS revenue,
           count(*)            AS order_count,
           max(po.created_at)  AS last_order_at
      FROM paid_orders po
     GROUP BY po.customer_id
)
SELECT tc.id,
       tc.email,
       tc.company,
       tc.country_code,
       a.revenue,
       a.order_count,
       a.last_order_at
  FROM agg a
  JOIN tenant_customers tc ON tc.id = a.customer_id
 WHERE a.last_order_at >= %(from)s
   AND a.last_order_at <  %(to)s
 ORDER BY a.revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

Het origineel joinde de aggregatie `totals` per rij opnieuw aan de laatste-order-set, wat ruim 48 miljoen rijen filterde. In deze versie worden omzet, aantal orders en laatste ordermoment in één GROUP BY berekend, nadat orders al tot de tenant zijn beperkt. Het resultaat blijft gelijk, omdat `max(created_at)` dezelfde waarde oplevert als `DISTINCT ON ... ORDER BY created_at DESC`.
